hub.title: Peer-to-peer webtools, armed with nostr.
hub.lead: Every tool here runs entirely in your browser and syncs over relays you choose. No sign-up needed, no server of ours, no tracking — and encryption happens before anything leaves your device.
hub.footer: Free software under the GPL — see the repository.
hub.relaysText: Every tool here syncs over these nostr relays; pick your own in the settings. Relays pass data along; they can’t read anything that was encrypted first. Photos and files go, encrypted, to your media servers.
hub.loadout.text: Grocery lists, to-dos, household inventory and markdown notes that sync between all your devices and whoever you share them with — rentry-style links, end-to-end encrypted. Works offline, and your devices put back whatever the relays forget.
hub.outpost.text: Grow reports and grow diaries: photos and notes from your grow, week by week, for everyone in Outpost, your friends, a circle or only you. Sealed on your device before anything leaves it; comments and likes from the people who can read them.
hub.tradingpost.text: A hemp marketplace: seeds, cuttings and gear, found by what they are and where they ship. Listings are sealed on your device; you write to sellers in Uplink. For people with an account.
hub.tradingpost.account: Trading Post is a hemp-related marketplace, so Armory keeps it for people with an account here.
hub.payload.text: Files to anyone: a link that waits on your media servers, encrypted, until you delete it; files to friends and groups in Uplink; or straight from your browser to theirs, stored nowhere. What came in Uplink is listed too.
hub.pongjs.text: Retro two-player Pong between two browsers. Share a link or QR code or pick an open game, then play over a direct connection, found through the relays.
hub.uplink.text: Messages to your friends, sealed on your device, and live rooms anyone with the link can join that vanish when they empty.
hub.devboard.text: A freelancer noticeboard: post that you’re hiring or available, signed with your key and backed by proof of work, voted on by peers, gone when it expires.
hub.calendar.text: Your calendar from your own Nextcloud or any CalDAV server: the coming days, a month, events that repeat, reminders. Nothing of it goes to relays; your login is sealed in your account.
hub.vault.text: A password manager: logins, notes, cards, two-factor codes, SSH keys and certificate authorities on every device you sign in on, with a generator, a health report and imports from other managers. Sealed with a passphrase of its own, which even your account’s password does not open.
hub.authenticator.text: Two-factor codes for your accounts elsewhere, on every device you sign in on. Add one with its QR code, its link or a Google Authenticator export; the secrets are sealed with a passphrase of their own, which even your account’s password does not open.
